rows.subtopic: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals
rows.stem: Copper is used for making cooking utensils. Which of the following physical properties of copper is NOT responsible for the same ?
rows.solution:
Copper is used for cooking utensils because it is malleable (it can be beaten into shape), it has a high melting point (it does not melt on the stove) and it is a good conductor of heat (it heats the food quickly and evenly). Copper is a metal of low reactivity, and that too suits utensils; high reactivity would make it react with food, water and air.

So the property that is not responsible is option (D) High reactivity.

rows.stem: Select endothermic reaction from the following :

options.label: A
options.text: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost.

options.label: B
options.text: Decomposition of calcium carbonate to form quick lime and carbon dioxide.

rows.solution:
An endothermic reaction absorbs energy. Calcium carbonate decomposes into quick lime and carbon dioxide only when it is heated strongly, so heat is absorbed:

\(\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CaO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost, burning of a candle and respiration all release energy, so they are exothermic.

This is option (B) Decomposition of calcium carbonate to form quick lime and carbon dioxide.

rows.stem: An electric iron of 1500 W, 200 V and a flash light of 500 W, 200 V are used in homes. The rating of fuse to be used should be
rows.solution:
The two appliances are used together, so the fuse must carry the total current.

Total power \(P = 1500 + 500 = 2000\) W, so \(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{2000}{200} = 10\) A.

This is option (B) 10 A.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The anaerobic respiration which takes place in yeast, has one of the end products as an acid.

**Reason (R) :** During anaerobic respiration, there is incomplete breakdown of glucose.
rows.context:
Q. Nos. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reason based questions.

These consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
In yeast, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) breaks pyruvate down into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Ethanol is an alcohol, not an acid (lactic acid is formed in our muscle cells, not in yeast), so the Assertion is false.

In anaerobic respiration glucose is not broken down completely to carbon dioxide and water, so less energy is released. The Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem: List two reasons to show that the existence of decomposers is essential in an ecosystem.
rows.solution:
Any two:

1. Decomposers break down the dead and decaying remains of plants and animals (organic matter) into simple inorganic substances.

2. These substances go back into the soil, so the nutrients in the soil are replenished naturally and can be used again by plants.

3. By removing dead bodies and wastes they keep the environment clean.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: A knife which is used to cut a fruit was immediately dipped into water containing drops of blue litmus solution. If the colour of the solution is changed to red, what inference can be drawn about the nature of the fruit and why ?
rows.solution: Blue litmus turns red in an acid. The juice of the fruit left on the knife dissolved in the water and turned the blue litmus red, so the fruit is acidic in nature.

rows.stem: Write the sequence of events that involve response of a person when a dust particle is inhaled through the nose by him.
rows.solution:
Sneezing is a reflex action. The sequence of events is:

Stimulus (the dust particle) \(\rightarrow\) Receptor (the nose) \(\rightarrow\) Sensory nerves \(\rightarrow\) Spinal cord \(\rightarrow\) Motor nerves \(\rightarrow\) Effector (the muscles of the nose) \(\rightarrow\) Response (sneezing)

The receptors in the nose detect the dust particle and send a message along the sensory nerves. The message is passed on to motor nerves, which carry it to the muscles, and the person sneezes, throwing the dust particle out. (The marking scheme's flow chart names the spinal cord; strictly, the sneeze reflex is coordinated in the medulla of the hind-brain, where the spinal cord joins the brain.)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
A person is suffering from an eye defect in which the far point of the eye is nearer than infinity. Identify the defect. List two main causes of this defect.

Draw a ray diagram to show how this defect is corrected by using a suitable lens.
rows.solution:
The defect is myopia (short-sightedness): the person can see nearby objects clearly but not distant ones, because the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina.

Two causes:

1. Excessive curvature of the eye lens.

2. Elongation of the eyeball.

It is corrected by a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power. Diagram: draw parallel rays from a distant object falling on a concave lens placed in front of the eye. The lens makes them diverge so that they appear to come from the far point O of the eye (mark this with dotted lines going back to O). The eye lens then converges these rays so that the image forms on the retina. Draw arrows on the rays.

rows.stem:
(a) The image of an object formed by a lens is of same size but inverted. If the object distance is 30 cm, calculate

(i) The distance between the object and its image.

(ii) Focal length of the lens.

(b) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formed in above case.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) For a lens, an image of the same size that is inverted is real, and it is formed only when the object is at 2F. So the object is at \(2F_1\), 30 cm in front of the lens, and the image is formed at \(2F_2\), 30 cm behind it, on the other side.

The distance between the object and its image is \(30 + 30 = 60\) cm.

(ii) The object is at 2F, so \(2f = 30\) cm and \(f = 15\) cm (a convex lens).

(Check with the lens formula: \(u = -30\) cm and \(v = +30\) cm, so \(\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{2}{30}\), giving \(f = 15\) cm.)

(b) Draw a convex lens with its principal axis, and mark \(F_1\) and \(2F_1\) on the left, \(F_2\) and \(2F_2\) on the right. Place the object AB at \(2F_1\). A ray from A parallel to the principal axis is refracted through \(F_2\); a ray from A through the optical centre O goes straight on. The two rays meet at A' below the axis at \(2F_2\). Draw A'B' perpendicular to the axis: the image is at \(2F_2\), real, inverted and of the same size as the object. Draw arrows on the rays.

rows.stem: Write the chemical composition of tooth enamel. Under what conditions of pH it starts corroding ? Explain the reason of tooth decay and suggest one method to prevent it.
rows.solution:
Tooth enamel is made of calcium hydroxyapatite, \(\mathrm{Ca_{10}(PO_4)_6(OH)_2}\), a crystalline form of calcium phosphate and the hardest substance in the body.

It starts corroding when the pH in the mouth falls below 5.5.

Bacteria present in the mouth degrade the sugar and the food particles left in the mouth after eating and produce acids. These acids lower the pH, react with the enamel and corrode it, which causes tooth decay.

To prevent it, clean the mouth after every meal, or brush the teeth with toothpaste, which is generally basic and neutralises the excess acid.

rows.stem:
(a) What happens when the egg is not fertilised ?

(b) How is sperm genetically different from a human egg / ova ?

(c) List any three contraceptive methods practised for family planning. Mention how these methods work.
rows.solution:
(a) If the egg is not fertilised, it lives for about one day. The lining of the uterus, which had become thick and spongy to receive a fertilised egg, is no longer needed. It breaks down slowly and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus. This is menstruation, which occurs roughly every month and lasts for about 2 to 8 days.

(b) A sperm carries either an X or a Y sex chromosome, while every human egg carries only an X chromosome. (Both are gametes with a single set of 23 chromosomes.) That is why the sperm decides the sex of the child.

(c) Any three:

1. Barrier method: a condom (or a diaphragm) prevents the sperm from reaching the egg, and the condom also protects against sexually transmitted diseases.

2. Oral pills: they change the hormonal balance of the body so that eggs are not released, and fertilisation cannot occur.

3. Surgical method: in a vasectomy the vas deferens of the male is blocked, so sperm transfer is prevented; in a tubectomy the fallopian tube of the female is blocked, so the egg cannot reach the uterus and fertilisation is prevented.

4. Intra-uterine devices such as the loop or copper-T are placed in the uterus and prevent pregnancy.
